title: VoIP Dialogs: Refactoring of singleton windows to factory methods
description:
Singletons moved from main_window to each class's static open<NameOfClass>
method:
- RtpPlayerDialog
- RtpStreamDialog
- VoipCallsDialog
- RtpAnalysisDialog

Fixed issue with selecting RTP stream in sequence dialog. When user
selected a stream and moved mouse to Rtp Player button and pressed it,
incorrect RTP stream was sent to the player.

I'm going to modify patch to include all telephone dialogs using singleton pattern.

Regarding documentation - I updated whole Telephony chapter, see https://www.wireshark.org/docs//wsug_html_chunked/ChTelPlayingCalls.html
Comments welcomed.

@ValZapod Just merged. Thank you.

This won't make it more painful to support multiple main windows (which we will need if we want to look even approximately like a native Mac application), will it?

Ideally, the notion that there's only one main window should ultimately be restricted to wireshark_application.{cpp, h}, so that most of the code won't need to be changed to support that.

Yes, but the original change (this MR is just refactoring) was about opening the only dialog for same task (limited to telephony). Before the change it opened e.g. multiple RTP streams dialogs and it was not possible to pass "signal" to correct one from other dialogs. Therefore I created dialog singletons and when you issue same action again, it just reuse existing dialog and all signals are routed to the dialog.
So I think it is something else than you mentioned regarding the Mac...

Once Wireshark is closer to a first-class Mac application, if you have two RTP capture files open at the same time, there will, on macOS, be only *one* process running the Wireshark executable (although we might have two subprocesses of that process doing the dissection and taps, one per file, with the UI process communicating with the two dissector processes).

What happens if the user opens an RTP streams dialog when the first file's window has the input focus, and then they select the second file's window, giving it the input focus, and open an RTP streams dialog?  Should that pop up a second RTP streams dialog, or just repurpose the single RTP streams dialog to hold the streams from the second file?

I see... I'm missing experience with Mac, but I will ask my team mates.

What I expect:

To process two files MAC must run two wireshark binaries/processes. Wireshark is not multithreaded nor "multifile" nowadays I thing. Dialog singleton is bound to process, so I expect it will open two RTP streams dialogs. But just two, one for each process/file.

Before my change, RTP Player dialog was modal so it was not possible to interact with rest of the application till Player window was closed. Did it worked in described scenario on Mac? I mean was possible to open two RTP Player dialogs - one per file? If so, my change works same way. The only change for RTP Player dialog is that it is not modal any more.

@graham.bloice Dear Graham, I think you have access to Mac. Can you check behaving in described scenario? Thank you in advance.

> To process two files MAC must run two wireshark binaries/processes.

"One top-level UI process per file" is an anti-pattern on macOS.  Things Just Aren't Done That Way.

That's why, for example, if you open a directory with multiple capture files in the Finder, double-click on one of them to open it in Wireshark, and then double-click on another one, instead of having both files open, the first file is no longer open and the window shows the second file.

That's *not* how apps are supposed to work on macOS - you're supposed to get a new window with a new file.

> Wireshark is not multithreaded nor "multifile" nowadays I thing.

It's not *now* multi-file on macOS.  That's a bug.

*Dissection* doesn't necessarily have to be multi-threaded; one possibility is to have a single UI process that talks to multiple "dissector" processes, where a "dissector" process first opens a file and reads it in, and then responds to "give me the summary information for packet N", "give me the protocol tree for packet N", "search for a packet that matches this expression and give me its packet number", "run this tap and give me the results", etc. requests.

That means we don't have to  have per-file data structures in the dissection code, and also means that we might be able to "sandbox" the dissector code so that it only gets file system, etc. access to files that the UI code lets it access, reducing the damage that can be caused by dissector bugs.

(Safari has a single UI process and multiple "Safari Web Content" processes, each one handling an open page.  See, for example, https://www.cultofmac.com/37374/apple-plans-chrome-like-safari-split-process-update/ and https://googleprojectzero.blogspot.com/2014/11/pwn4fun-spring-2014-safari-part-ii.html.

And, yes, as the second paper shows, sandboxing isn't magic that makes security problems go away.)

> Did it worked in described scenario on Mac? I mean was possible to open two RTP Player dialogs - one per file?

It was - and is - not possible for a Wireshark process to have more than one file open, so the answer to that question is "the question is not well-formed".

When we make Wireshark work more like a first-class Mac app, it *should* be possible to have multiple files open, and it should be possible to have at least one RTP player dialog per file.

Currently, to have more than one file open in Wireshark on macOS, you have to manually launch Wireshark on files other than the first file, which will put multiple Wireshark icons in the Dock (not a good sign).  Each of those would be able to have its own RTP dialogs; we shouldn't lose that capability when we make Wireshark work more like a first-class Mac app.

I understand Mac goal, but I can't change it with this part of the code. My change didn't improved nor deteriorated it from this point of view.

Question I forgot to ask any Mac user, but it looks important in this case and confuses me personally:
Imagine Wireshark is first-class Mac app. I open two files and it shows just one window or one icon in launcher, but two windows?
I mean that as a user I need to be able to see two windows in row to see two captures to e.g. compare/find difference between them by my eyes. Is it possible?
What happens (should happen) if you open two windows for each capture - e.g. main window and RTP player and again I want to see two players on the screen?

> Question I forgot to ask any Mac user, but it looks important in this case and confuses me personally: Imagine Wireshark is first-class Mac app. I open two files and it shows just one window

No, it shows two windows.

> or one icon in launcher, but two windows?

One icon in the Dock, two windows.

> I mean that as a user I need to be able to see two windows in row to see two captures to e.g. compare/find difference between them by my eyes. Is it possible?

Yes.

Double-click on one capture, or run the command `open {capture file path}` from a terminal window, or (if you already have a Wireshark window open) do File > Open and choose a file, and a window will pop up for the file (or, if the file is already open, the window for it will move to the front and get the input focus).

Then do that on another capture file, and another window will be opened (or, again, moved to the front and given the input focus).

> What happens (should happen) if you open two windows for each capture - e.g. main window and RTP player

[The Apple Human Interface Guidelines for macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/macos/overview/themes/) have [a "Window Anatomy" page](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/macos/windows-and-views/window-anatomy/) with a "Types of Windows".  None of the types in that list obviously correspond to windows such as the RTP dialogs; the closest match appears to be [a Panel window](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/macos/windows-and-views/panels/).

Many of the Panels they describe are really just more persistent versions of pop-up dialogs, e.g. "Show Fonts" and "Show Colors"; that doesn't match analysis dialogs.

Inspectors are maybe a little closer, but the closest may be Info windows:

> An Info window is a standard window that displays content attributes (sometimes for multiple items) captured at the time the window was opened. These attributes continue to be displayed even when the selection changes. Unlike inspectors, Info windows appear in the Window menu’s document list, don’t float above other windows, can be minimized, and may remain visible when the app becomes inactive.

But the example they give in the screenshot ("General Info", probably from the Preview PDF/image viewer app) is probably closest to the Statistics > Capture File Properties window.  The problem here may be that the windows popped up by stuff under Analyze, Statistics, Telephony, etc. are "pro app" types of dialogs, and the only "pro apps" I have are Xcode and, err, umm, Wireshark.

I'm not very familiar with Xcode, as my development environment is "Terminal, microEmacs, and the command line".  Creating a tiny "hello, world" project, I did manage to get an "Analyze" window, which may be equivalent to some analysis dialogs Wireshark pops up, but it seems different for an Info window, as it's *not* in the Window menu's document list, even though it doesn't float above other windows and can be minimized.  One analysis display, Energy Impact, seems to be shown in the *main* window as a *tab*, with no obvious option to make it a separate window.

In any case, they don't explicitly say so, but I suspect that having (at least) one Info window, or whatever, per document, in a document-oriented app (which Wireshark is), would be allowed.

So there could be one RTP player dialog per window.

Thank you for links and explanation. I think that we/wireshark can't do more than Qt framework does.
I will study this topic more...

> I think that we/wireshark can't do more than Qt framework does.

As far as I know, what the Qt frameworks supports includes "Mac applications that have one process managing multiple open documents in multiple document windows".

We'd need to respond to [`QFileOpenEvent` events](https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qfileopenevent.html), for example - and *not* by closing any files, but by leaving all existing files open and opening a new one.

I discussed the topic with my Mac teammates. They explained me what is consequence of one application with two windows vs. two applications with one window:

Mac UI allows you to place windows on multiple desktops and then show you where the application has windows placed. If there are two separate applications, it shows you where window is, but you must know that you have two applications and must click on right application. It has a lot consequences for gestures etc. too.
So it is clear to me why it is so important...

What I suggest is to finish discussion there and add Wiki page with requirements for Mac UI. When there will be anyone who will be interested in implementation, they will have requirements to follow.
So I was testing it this month, works good.
I'm happy to hear it. Thank you for your help.
